title: Three enforced invariants: worktree-correct gate reads, binder validity at commit time, and a register checker
summary: Narrows three gaps the invariant register names as open: the landing gate judges the worktree a merge actually runs in instead of the primary checkout; a binder that a commit is about to record is schema-validated, not only checked for review freshness; and a new checker verifies that every register entry's carrier files, quoted phrases, and named enforcement scripts still exist. Every touched register entry and backlog item flips in the same diff to its honest post-change status — enforced where enforced, partial with every remainder named where not.
motivation: Register entries INV-11, INV-7, and INV-20 each name their gap plainly; backlog items 11 and 21 carry two of the fix shapes, and the third was named directly by the register when it landed. This binder builds the state-read and commit-time halves without the route gate, which a later binder builds on top of this one's resolver. The three items are delivered as one integration branch, so an intermediate state between items never lands alone.

included: scripts/hooks/_worktree.py (new) — the shared invocation-root resolver both hooks consume: resolve_invocation_root(cwd) -> Path | None with walk-up containment semantics scoped to THIS repository, import-safe, stdlib-only, with its own --self-test and named cases

scripts/hooks/roundtable_gate.py — the landing gate and every other lookup in the decision resolve from the invoking worktree via one rescope call site at the top of the decision, with the denial for an unacceptable cwd deferred to where it fires today; contradictory ordering comments corrected

scripts/hooks/precommit_gate.py — a binder-validity step validating, per commit shape, exactly the bytes that commit would record, the register checker joining a re-rooted gate list, and the timeout budget re-balanced to pinned, derived constants

skills/karta-plan/scripts/validate_binder.py — a --no-cross-binder flag for isolated single-binder validation, and malformed input (bad JSON, bad encoding) reported as a normal INVALID finding instead of a traceback

scripts/check_invariant_register.py (new) — parses the register under a pinned grammar and verifies carriers, phrases, and named enforcement scripts against a --root tree, with verdict/crash exit codes

docs/conventions/invariants.md — same-diff status flips: INV-11 (item one), INV-7 (item two), INV-20 and the How-this-file-stays-true section (item three); the flips items one and two write conform to item three's pinned grammar shapes
docs/backlog/README.md — item 11's status (item one) and item 21's status (item three)

AGENTS.md — the landing-gate residual sentence (item one) and the Before-you-commit floor paragraph updated to the post-change gate list (item three); both edits keep every phrase the register quotes from the edited sections intact or update the register's quote in the same diff
excluded: The route gate that would block an ordinary direct commit to the default branch (register INV-17) — a later binder builds it on this resolver

Backlog item 22's fix — accepting git -C <worktree> command shapes. This binder only makes state reads worktree-correct for shapes the gates already accept; -C relocation and cd-chains remain named residuals, not silent ones

Compound commands that mutate binder bytes between the hook's read and the commit, and glob or magic pathspecs beyond deterministic expansion — named residual bounds in item two's doc comment and INV-7's flip, not closed
Cross-binder validation at commit time (slug collisions, after-edge resolution) — deliberately skipped by --no-cross-binder and named as a remainder in INV-7's flip

Staged-versus-working-tree divergence for the register checker — it reads the tree the gate suite runs in, the same bound every gate in the suite shares; named as a remainder in INV-20's flip, not closed
No UI surface: no design_reference, component_map, icon_map, token_changes, or token_manifest anywhere in this binder

design_facts.stack: Python-stdlib tooling repo (hooks, validators, skills); no manifests, no CI workflows — the floor is the repo's own validator suite

work_items.title: The landing gate reads the worktree it was invoked in
work_items.summary: Extract one shared resolver for the invocation root and put it in effect for the whole gate decision at a single call site, so a merge run from a linked worktree is judged on that worktree's state instead of the primary checkout's — correcting what the landing gate reads without changing which working directories it accepts.
work_items.contract: PROBLEM (register INV-11, backlog item 11): decide() resolves the invoking cwd and rescopes its (git, read_file, is_symlink) triple at the _check_cwd step, which runs AFTER the early part of decide() — and the LANDING gate runs in that early part, deliberately ahead of both the skip hatch and the config switch. So the landing gate's branch checks read the PRIMARY checkout, never the worktree the merge runs in; backlog item 11 demonstrated the false block and the inverted false pass. The deliver-merge review gate already reads the rebound git after the 5b14c49 rescope and must not regress. WHAT CHANGES AND WHAT DOES NOT, precisely: this item never changes which working directories are accepted or denied — _check_cwd keeps its acceptance set, reason text, and firing position. It changes what the landing gate READS, which deliberately corrects both observed decision errors: a real landing whose worktree HEAD is the default branch now blocks (the false negative becomes a correct denial), and an integration-to-integration consolidation run from a worktree no longer blocks (the false positive becomes a correct pass). SHARED MODULE: extract the cwd-to-root resolution into NEW scripts/hooks/_worktree.py — import surface pinned as resolve_invocation_root(cwd: str) -> pathlib.Path | None with WALK-UP CONTAINMENT semantics scoped to this repository: any cwd inside the primary working tree returns ROOT, any cwd inside a linked worktree OF THIS REPOSITORY returns that worktree's top level, and anything else — outside any repository, or inside a different repository — returns None. The resolver decides where state is read, never whether a cwd is acceptable — acceptance stays _check_cwd's job on the original payload cwd, and _check_cwd delegates its own root DISCOVERY to this same module so discovery can never disagree; that delegation, and the acceptance asymmetry it leaves intact, are together a named suite case. Import-safe (no module-level side effects, __main__ guard), stdlib-only, own --self-test ending in an N/N checks passed line with these five case names on [PASS] lines: root-cwd-returns-root, worktree-top-returns-worktree, subdir-returns-containing-top, outside-returns-none, other-repo-returns-none. The second module is justified by its second consumer: precommit_gate.py imports it in the next item, and importing the 2600-line review hook cross-file was rejected. roundtable_gate.py keeps its own rescope machinery (the git/read_file/is_symlink adapters stay hook-local — the two hooks use incompatible git result types) but derives the root through the shared module. HOIST WITH DEFERRED DENIAL, position pinned: the resolver fires at the top of decide(), after payload parsing and the basic shape checks that return 0 for non-judged invocations, and BEFORE the landing-gate branch's first current_branch read — so one resolved triple is observed by the landing branch, the config reads, _check_cwd's delegated discovery, and both sub-dispatches. The existing later rescope line (the 'if effective != str(ROOT)' site) is REMOVED in this diff: the hoist is the single rescope call site, and double-rescoping an already-adapted triple is thereby impossible. Resolve lazily, at most once per decide() invocation and only for invocations the gate judges (a commit, a merge, or a landing-gate candidate — never for shapes that return 0 before any gate today), memoizing the result; the accepted cost is up to one rev-parse-shaped subprocess per judged invocation and is named here. Rescope ONLY when the resolved root differs from ROOT — a ROOT-cwd invocation keeps the triple it was handed, so the existing stub-driven cases are undisturbed. On a cwd that resolves to None, DO NOT deny early: keep the ROOT triple for the landing-gate evaluation exactly as today, and let _check_cwd raise its existing Denial at its current position. SUITE CASES, all named verbatim as the message string of a real check() invocation (a name that exists only in a comment is not a case — the acceptance gate verifies this against the diff): landing-worktree-false-positive and landing-worktree-false-negative (on pre-fix code both fail because the landing gate reads the primary checkout's stubbed HEAD — the stated reason matches why they fail, house.4), skip-hatch-subdir-cwd-merge-allowed, payload-without-cwd-unchanged, worktree-head-config-divergence, resolver-check-cwd-agreement (two facts on one fixture list: _check_cwd's root discovery returns exactly the resolver's answer for every fixture, and every None-resolving cwd is denied — while acceptance stays _check_cwd's own decision on the original cwd, so a subdirectory fixture resolves for reads and is still denied; discovery delegation and acceptance independence, never set equality). The suite's rescope seam stays injectable (rescope=None defaulting to the real one) so these cases drive stubs, never real worktrees — the self-test must not mutate the repository's own worktree registry. CONFIG READS MOVE WITH THE RESCOPE: head_config and _first_enable_possible read the resolved worktree's HEAD after the hoist — a deliberate, named semantic change (the gate judges the tree the commit or merge is actually about): a worktree whose HEAD config disables review is now honored where the primary's config would have enforced it, pinned by worktree-head-config-divergence; the INV-11 flip and the AGENTS.md residual sentence both name this behavior change. COMMENTS: the file's two ordering comments contradict each other (the landing gate says it runs ahead of the skip hatch; the skip hatch says it is evaluated before every other rule) — correct them to the enforced order in this same diff. MEASURED BASELINE: python3 scripts/hooks/roundtable_gate.py --self-test printed 1794/1794 checks passed at plan time (2026-09-01, repo root); after this item the suite must be fully green with at least 1800 checks — the baseline plus the six named cases; the floor is a tripwire against outright omission, and the acceptance gate's diff verification is what proves each named case is a real check() invocation. BENCHMARKS: benchmarks/gate/run_gate.py probes do not reference roundtable_gate.py (verified at plan time; re-verify at build), so benchmarks/results/gate needs no refresh. SAME-DIFF DOC FLIPS (inv.1), written in the grammar item three pins: (a) register INV-11 stays **partial** — state reads are now worktree-correct for resolvable payload cwds — with TWO named remainders — the cd-chain shape (where a shell command finally runs is not decidable from command text; the observed 2026-08-24 false block was this shape and payload-cwd resolution does not fix it) and backlog item 22's -C relocation — plus the worktree-HEAD config reads named as a DELIBERATE behavior change, not a gap; Carriers gain scripts/hooks/_worktree.py; (b) docs/backlog/README.md item 11's heading flips to '*Fixed for payload-cwd invocations (2026-09-01)*' with the cd/-C remainder pointed at item 22 — never a bare FIXED (the deliberate casing difference from the file's '*FIXED' convention marks it partial); (c) AGENTS.md's landing-gate limits gain a residual sentence containing verbatim the fragments 'not decidable from command text', 'cd-chain', and 'git -C', and noting the config-divergence change; the edit keeps every phrase the register quotes from that section intact or updates the register's quote in the same diff. FAIL-OPEN / DENY-BY-NAME (INV-21): _check_cwd's Denial keeps its reason text and position; hook_main's blanket fail-open stands; no new internal-error path may deny. RE-VERIFY AT BUILD: resolver-vs-_check_cwd discovery delegation, worktree membership decided by comparing the cwd tree's git common directory with ROOT's (the rev-parse --git-common-dir shape, or the .git pointer-file equivalent — never a nearest-git-root heuristic that a different repository could satisfy), the exact current line positions, the benchmarks claim, and that the suite prints its summary as 'N/N checks passed'.

oracle.command: sh -c 'set -e; OUT=$(python3 scripts/hooks/roundtable_gate.py --self-test 2>&1); printf %s "$OUT" | tail -3; printf %s "$OUT" | python3 -c "import re,sys; s=sys.stdin.read(); m=re.search(r\"(\\d+)/(\\d+) checks passed\", s); assert m and m.group(1)==m.group(2), (\"suite not fully green\", s[-300:]); assert int(m.group(1)) >= 1800, \"below 1800 = measured 1794 baseline plus the six named cases\""; for c in landing-worktree-false-positive landing-worktree-false-negative skip-hatch-subdir-cwd-merge-allowed payload-without-cwd-unchanged worktree-head-config-divergence resolver-check-cwd-agreement; do grep -q "$c" scripts/hooks/roundtable_gate.py; done; WOUT=$(python3 scripts/hooks/_worktree.py --self-test 2>&1); printf %s "$WOUT" | python3 -c "import re,sys; s=sys.stdin.read(); m=re.search(r\"(\\d+)/(\\d+) checks passed\", s); assert m and m.group(1)==m.group(2) and int(m.group(1)) >= 5, (\"_worktree self-test not green or under 5 cases\", s[-300:])"; for c in root-cwd-returns-root worktree-top-returns-worktree subdir-returns-containing-top outside-returns-none other-repo-returns-none; do printf %s "$WOUT" | grep -q "\\[PASS\\].*$c"; done; sed -n "/^## 11\\./,/^## 12\\./p" docs/backlog/README.md | grep -q "Fixed for payload-cwd invocations"; INV=$(sed -n "/### INV-11/,/### INV-12/p" docs/conventions/invariants.md); printf %s "$INV" | grep -q "item 22"; printf %s "$INV" | grep -q "\\*\\*partial\\*\\*"; printf %s "$INV" | grep -q "_worktree.py"; printf %s "$INV" | grep -qi "config"; grep -qF "not decidable from command text" AGENTS.md; grep -qF "cd-chain" AGENTS.md; grep -qF "git -C" AGENTS.md; PV=$(python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test 2>&1); printf %s "$PV" | grep -qF "PLUGIN INTEGRITY: PASS"; echo "RESOLVER ORACLE OK"'
assertions: roundtable_gate.py --self-test is fully green (parsed from stdin, never argv — the output exceeds a single argument's size limit) with at least 1800 checks: the measured 1794 baseline plus the six named cases, so the floor catches an omitted case; each named case must be the message string of a real check() invocation, a final-text property the acceptance gate confirms against the diff

the six named cases cover both landing directions (failing on pre-fix code because the landing gate reads the primary checkout's stubbed HEAD), the skip-hatch subdirectory allowance, the payload-without-cwd preservation, the config-divergence pin, and the resolver-vs-_check_cwd agreement
_worktree.py's own self-test is green with at least its five named cases each on a [PASS] line — walk-up semantics proven at all boundaries including a different repository

backlog item 11's own section carries 'Fixed for payload-cwd invocations'; INV-11's section shows **partial**, names item 22, the config change, and _worktree.py as a carrier; AGENTS.md contains all three pinned residual fragments verbatim
validate_plugin.py --self-test output contains PLUGIN INTEGRITY: PASS, checked on captured output rather than a pipe's exit status

work_items.title: A commit recording an invalid binder is blocked
work_items.summary: Add a commit-hook step that validates, for each commit shape, exactly the live binder bytes that commit would record — staged blobs for plain commits, working-tree bytes for staging shapes, untracked files a broad add covers — under a bounded end-to-end budget, so a hand-edited invalid binder can no longer be committed.
work_items.contract: PROBLEM (register INV-7, status partial): freshness is enforced — the review gate hashes the staged binder bytes — but schema validity is not, so a hand-edited invalid binder can still be committed. TRIGGER: the step fires only on a true commit subcommand — the detection must use a boundary that excludes commit-tree and commit-graph (backlog item 10's false-fire examples, pinned here as the negative case binder-commit-tree-not-gated) even though the hook's broader is_commit_command may still over-match for the purpose of running the read-only gate suite. LIVE BINDER PATHS: any path under .karta/binders/ at any depth ending .json whose normalized path does not start with .karta/binders/archive/ — matched by prefix and suffix, never a single-star glob (which cannot cross a slash: the dead-code trap). CANDIDATES AND BYTES, PER COMMIT SHAPE — validate exactly what that shape records, never more: (1) PLAIN COMMIT (no -a, no pathspec, no chained add): candidates are the staged live binder paths from git diff --cached --name-status -z at the resolved root; bytes are the index blobs (git show :<path>). (2) PATHSPEC COMMIT: git records the named paths' WORKING-TREE state and leaves other staged changes out — candidates are only the live binder paths deterministically covered by the pathspecs (exact paths and directory prefixes; globs and magic pathspecs are a named residual), bytes are working-tree; a staged-but-uncovered binder is NOT a candidate, because this commit does not record it. (3) -a COMMIT: staged candidates as in (1) plus tracked-modified live binders from git diff --name-status -z, with working-tree bytes winning for any path in both sets. (4) CHAINED git add THEN commit in one command: candidates additionally include live binder paths covered by the add arguments — exact paths, directory prefixes, '.', -A/--all, and the update family -u/--update (which covers tracked-modified live binders exactly as -a does, D exempt) — including UNTRACKED files under covered prefixes (never under -u, which stages no untracked file) enumerated via git ls-files --others --exclude-standard restricted to .karta/binders/; bytes are working-tree. PATHSPEC AND ADD ARGUMENTS RESOLVE AGAINST THE PAYLOAD CWD: joined and normalized to repo-relative before coverage matching, so a subdirectory-relative spec matches the binder it actually names. MIXED SHAPES: a commit carrying --include/-i records the index PLUS the named paths and validates the union — staged candidates as in (1) plus covered working-tree candidates, working-tree bytes winning; --only takes shape (2); a --dry-run commit records nothing and never triggers the step. The step's positive trigger set is the hook's existing commit detection minus the excluded commit-tree and commit-graph subcommands — --amend included. SYMLINKS: working-tree bytes for a symlinked binder path are the link text git would record as the blob, never the target's contents. DELETIONS: a D status is the sole exemption in EVERY enumeration above, staged or working-tree — a deleted binder is never read, and a worktree deletion under -a or a covered add is exempt, not a missing-file error. Statuses are classified by first letter (score suffixes like R100 stripped); the DESTINATION path of R and C validates. The enumeration returns an inspectable (candidates, exempted) pair so self-test cases assert an archive or deleted path was CONSIDERED and exempted, never merely not-denied. NAMED RESIDUAL BOUNDS, stated in the step's doc comment and in INV-7's flip: git -C relocation (backlog item 22's territory), post-read mutation by compound commands, non-deterministic pathspecs and -f/--force adds of ignored paths, cross-binder checks skipped by --no-cross-binder, and commits that arrive by merge, rebase, or cherry-pick — no commit subcommand fires the step, the same accepted-bypass family AGENTS.md names for the review gates. VALIDATOR INVOCATION: materialize each candidate's bytes into its own fresh tempfile.TemporaryDirectory (one per candidate, so equal basenames cannot collide) as <basename>.json and run [sys.executable] skills/karta-plan/scripts/validate_binder.py --binder <path> --no-cross-binder with cwd set to the resolved root. BUDGET, end-to-end: 50 seconds covers the whole step — enumeration git calls, materialization, and validator subprocesses — timed from the step's first git call and checked between candidates, each validator invocation limited to the remaining balance; on exhaustion the step fails OPEN with a warning naming the budget and the unvalidated repo paths. DENIAL: names the step and the candidate's REPO-RELATIVE path — the step keeps a basename-to-repo-path map so the validator's output tail (which sees only the temp basename) is reported against the real path — with the tail via _tail(). VALIDATE_BINDER CHANGES, this same item: (1) NEW flag --no-cross-binder skips sibling-glob and archive discovery while keeping every single-binder check; (2) malformed input (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, unreadable file) is caught and reported as a normal INVALID finding with a nonzero exit, never a traceback, and every findings report opens with a distinctive sentinel line only the findings printer can emit — unreachable from any crash path; (3) its self-test gains cases named validator-no-cross-binder-isolated and validator-malformed-json-invalid on [PASS] lines; measured baseline 75/75 at plan time, so at least 77 after. CRASH IS NOT A VERDICT: deny only when the validator exits nonzero AND its output carries the findings sentinel above; a traceback, a missing validator, a spawn failure, or budget exhaustion fails OPEN with a warning, and the crash case asserts crash output LACKS the sentinel, so a crash can never masquerade as a finding. No candidate means the step is skipped, not run-and-passed. KARTA_SKIP_GATE=1 bypasses this step exactly as it bypasses the gate suite. SUITE CASES, each the message string of a real check() invocation (a name in a comment is not a case — the acceptance gate verifies this against the diff): binder-invalid-staged-denied (stating which validator rule its fixture violates, house.4), binder-valid-staged-passes, binder-archive-exempt (considered-then-exempted via the inspectable pair), binder-delete-exempt, binder-staging-shape-worktree-bytes, binder-staging-shape-delete-exempt, binder-pathspec-worktree-bytes, binder-pathspec-scope-restricted (a staged invalid binder NOT covered by the pathspec does not deny that commit), binder-chained-add-worktree-bytes, binder-chained-add-update-denied, binder-untracked-broad-add-denied (an invalid untracked binder under git add -A or add . is denied), binder-untracked-not-staged-passes (an untracked binder no add covers never denies), binder-copy-destination-validated, binder-malformed-json-denied, binder-blob-read-fail-open, binder-validator-crash-fail-open, binder-step-resolved-root, binder-commit-tree-not-gated, binder-skip-hatch-bypass. MEASURED BASELINE: precommit_gate.py --self-test printed 47/47 at plan time; after this item it must be fully green with at least 66 checks — the baseline plus the nineteen named cases; the floor is a tripwire against outright omission, and the acceptance gate's diff verification is what proves each named case is a real check() invocation. SAME-DIFF DOC FLIP (inv.1), written in the grammar item three pins: register INV-7 flips to **partial** with the post-change truth — schema validity enforced at commit for the per-shape byte sources above — and FIVE named remainders: -C relocation, post-read mutation by compound commands, non-deterministic pathspecs and forced adds of ignored paths, cross-binder checks skipped at commit time, and merge arrival (merge, rebase, cherry-pick fire no commit subcommand); Carriers gain scripts/hooks/precommit_gate.py; the old clause 'the commit hook does not run it' is removed. RE-VERIFY AT BUILD: precommit_gate.py's git cwd behavior, validate_binder.py's exact findings marker and that no single-binder check depends on the binder's on-disk location, and the hook's actual commit detection against the commit-tree/commit-graph examples.

oracle.command: sh -c 'set -e; OUT=$(python3 scripts/hooks/precommit_gate.py --self-test 2>&1); printf %s "$OUT" | tail -3; printf %s "$OUT" | python3 -c "import re,sys; s=sys.stdin.read(); m=re.search(r\"(\\d+)/(\\d+) checks passed\", s); assert m and m.group(1)==m.group(2), (\"suite not fully green\", s[-300:]); assert int(m.group(1)) >= 66, \"below 66 = measured 47 baseline plus the nineteen named cases\""; for c in binder-invalid-staged-denied binder-valid-staged-passes binder-archive-exempt binder-delete-exempt binder-staging-shape-worktree-bytes binder-staging-shape-delete-exempt binder-pathspec-worktree-bytes binder-pathspec-scope-restricted binder-chained-add-worktree-bytes binder-chained-add-update-denied binder-untracked-broad-add-denied binder-untracked-not-staged-passes binder-copy-destination-validated binder-malformed-json-denied binder-blob-read-fail-open binder-validator-crash-fail-open binder-step-resolved-root binder-commit-tree-not-gated binder-skip-hatch-bypass; do grep -q "$c" scripts/hooks/precommit_gate.py; done; VOUT=$(python3 skills/karta-plan/scripts/validate_binder.py --self-test 2>&1); printf %s "$VOUT" | python3 -c "import re,sys; s=sys.stdin.read(); m=re.search(r\"(\\d+)/(\\d+) checks passed\", s); assert m and m.group(1)==m.group(2), (\"validator suite not fully green\", s[-300:]); assert int(m.group(1)) >= 77, \"below 77 = measured 75 baseline plus the two named cases\""; for c in validator-no-cross-binder-isolated validator-malformed-json-invalid; do printf %s "$VOUT" | grep -q "\\[PASS\\].*$c"; done; INV=$(sed -n "/### INV-7/,/### INV-8/p" docs/conventions/invariants.md); printf %s "$INV" | grep -q "\\*\\*partial\\*\\*"; printf %s "$INV" | grep -q "precommit_gate"; printf %s "$INV" | grep -qi "cross-binder"; printf %s "$INV" | grep -qi "pathspec"; printf %s "$INV" | grep -qF "git -C"; printf %s "$INV" | grep -qiE "post-read|compound"; printf %s "$INV" | grep -qi "merge"; ! printf %s "$INV" | grep -qF "the commit hook does not run it"; echo "BINDER-VALIDITY ORACLE OK"'
assertions: precommit_gate.py --self-test is fully green with at least 66 checks — the measured 47 baseline plus the nineteen named cases; each named case must be the message string of a real check() invocation, a final-text property the acceptance gate confirms against the diff

the nineteen named cases cover every per-shape byte source both directions: staged denial and pass-through, considered-then-exempted archive and deletion paths in both enumerations, all three staging shapes, pathspec scope restriction (no denial for uncovered staged binders), broad-add untracked denial and no-add untracked pass, the copy destination, malformed JSON as a verdict, both fail-open paths, the resolved-root plumb, the commit-tree non-trigger, and the skip hatch
validate_binder.py's own suite is fully green at or above 77 with its two named cases on [PASS] lines — the isolation flag works and malformed JSON is a finding, not a traceback
INV-7's section shows **partial**, carries precommit_gate as a carrier, names all five remainders including merge arrival, and no longer contains the old 'the commit hook does not run it' clause

the fail-open bounds hold: budget exhaustion, validator crash, spawn failure, and unreadable blobs never deny; only a real validation finding on successfully materialized bytes does, reported against the repo-relative path

work_items.title: The register's carriers are checked, not just asserted
work_items.summary: Add a checker that parses the invariant register under a pinned grammar, confirms every entry's carrier file exists with its quoted phrase present and every named enforcement script real, wire it into a re-rooted commit-gate list under derived timeout constants, and update the register's claims about itself in the same change.
work_items.contract: PROBLEM (register INV-20, its How-this-file-stays-true section, backlog item 21): the register names each entry's carriers as a file plus a distinctive quoted phrase and states plainly that no checker verifies them — proven exposed the day the register landed, when a sibling delivery rewrote a carrier paragraph and only a lucky merge conflict surfaced it. NEW FILE scripts/check_invariant_register.py, stdlib-only argparse with --root <path> (default '.') and --self-test per house.2 ([PASS]/[FAIL] lines, each case name on its [PASS] line, ending with a required 'N/N checks passed' summary line). EXIT CODES, pinned: 0 all entries pass; 1 verification or parse failure with named reasons — a --root with no register file at docs/conventions/invariants.md is itself a named exit-1 failure, never a silent pass or a crash; 2 internal crash. The hook denies ONLY on exit 1; exit 2, a timeout, or a spawn failure fails OPEN with a warning, pinned by hook cases register-crash-fail-open and register-timeout-fail-open. Say the posture honestly: a CRASH never blocks anyone (INV-21), while a malformed or drifted register denying by name is the design — the register is doctrine, and a broken doctrine file blocking a commit is exactly what a drifted mirror already does in this suite. PINNED GRAMMAR — a parse failure is a named exit-1 denial citing entry id and line number, never a guess: an entry heading is a line beginning '### INV-'; one that does not match the full shape '### INV-<digits> · <title>', and any duplicate id, is itself a named parse failure (near-misses fail loudly, never vanish). Bullet continuation lines (indented) are joined to their bullet before parsing. The status line is the first bullet whose bold token is exactly one of enforced, partial, prose, prose by design — matched longest-first; an entry with no status bullet at all is a named parse failure. The Carriers bullet begins '- Carriers:'; its value splits on '; ' ONLY where the split point is outside double quotes and outside parentheses; each resulting segment must contain exactly ONE carrier file token (zero or two-plus is a named parse failure; a script-pattern token counts as the segment's carrier token when it is the only file-shaped token — INV-20's own carrier is exactly that shape) plus zero or more ASCII double-quoted phrases, every one of which must appear in that segment's file; a Carriers value beginning 'none yet' names no file and is a structural pass ONLY for an entry whose status is prose or prose by design — on an enforced or partial entry it is a named verification failure, because an enforced claim with no carrier is the drift this checker exists to catch; an entry with no Carriers bullet at all is a named parse failure. TOKEN RULES: file and script tokens are repo-relative path-shaped tokens — no leading slash, no '..' segments (either is a named parse failure) — recognized inside backticks or bare; EXTRACTION ORDER pinned: quoted phrases are extracted first and masked, so file and script tokens are collected only from unmasked text — a path inside a quoted phrase is never a token; backtick and markdown-link stripping applies ONLY to token extraction, while quoted phrases are taken verbatim between their quotes, backticks included.
